title: A full fleet still moved the rotation cursor to the read's last project, so backlogs drained first in, first out
resolution: A decline for lack of fleet capacity (quarantine, worker eligibility or capacity, no candidate) no longer counts as an offer; with nothing placed the cursor stops before the first one; contract, spec, and design state it.

title: The outage test passed with the cursor left unmoved or the failed offer counted, because the first project had no task left
resolution: Added a later task of the first project to the outage test and a test of an outage at the first offer with a cursor set; both fail on temporary mutants of those two defects.

title: The no-candidate test started without a cursor, so resetting the cursor would pass
resolution: The test now sets the cursor with a placing pass before the pass without a candidate; it fails on a mutant that resets the cursor.

title: The pass runner discarded each pass result, so an unexpected failure went unnoticed
resolution: runPass checks every pass result: ok for the normal passes, a failure for the expected outage.

title: The offer loop mutated a cursor passed in and also answered the placement count
resolution: #offer(order, after) builds the cursor and returns the count or the outage with the next cursor; #placeDue stores it.

title: Contract section 5 said the rotation starts after the project that last received capacity, untrue after a pass that placed nothing
resolution: Section 5 now says the rotation starts after the rotation cursor that item 18 fixes.

title: The placement queue port comment still said the caller passes the last project read
resolution: The comment now says that passing the rotation cursor reaches P blocked projects in ceil(P/limit) reads.

title: The rotation requirement did not say that an offer the store failed does not count
resolution: The requirement now says an offer the store failed does not count.

title: The per-task backoff after a capacity decline lets the project whose backoff ends first take a freed slot, so the rotation degrades under jitter
resolution: Not a regression and contract section 5 requires the backoff; the design and the record state the limit, and the follow-up change placement-backoff-preserves-rotation takes option (a), no task backoff after a fleet capacity decline, as chosen by the owner's delegate.

title: The proposal still stated the cursor rule from before review pass 1
resolution: The proposal now states the rule of the design and the contract, a full fleet at the first offer included.

title: The rotation requirement said before a decline where the contract says before the first decline
resolution: The requirement now says before its first decline for lack of fleet capacity.

title: A slot freed later in a pass placed a later project and moved the cursor past projects declined for fleet capacity
resolution: The cursor moves only by the offers before the first fleet capacity decline, even when a later offer is placed; contract, spec, design, and a service test state it.

title: The fleet capacity check sees only the last candidate's reason, so control-not-enforceable can hide a full worker once hard controls exist
resolution: Recorded in the design risks: G2 requests no hard control, and the case matters once hard controls exist.

title: The rotation cursor API depended on the call order of offered, placed, and ranOutOfCapacity
resolution: RotationCursor takes one exclusive event per offer: placed, declined, or ranOutOfCapacity.

title: No service test covered a decline after a capacity decline in a pass without placement, or a transaction without a candidate
resolution: Added both service tests; they fail on mutants that drop the cut-off or the no-candidate reason.

title: The fleet capacity check had two names across layers and no-candidate sat outside the fleet reasons; the offer result field named placed held an outage too
resolution: The service uses lacksFleetCapacity from the domain, whose FLEET_REASONS include NO_CANDIDATE_REASON; the field is outcome.
